title: Keep project frontend context evidence-backed and local
principle: For an existing product, keep an optional project-local frontend context that records inspected system evidence and behavior constraints; use it to guide refinement without turning historical taste into a universal theme.
rationale: Agents make safer, more coherent changes when they can distinguish verified tokens, component ownership, platform behavior, and rejected patterns from temporary requests or aesthetic guesses.
applies_when: A maintained product has repeated frontend work, a design system, platform-specific interaction conventions, or a history of accepted and rejected visual decisions.
exceptions: Do not create a durable manifest for a one-off fix unless it captures a stable, reviewable product decision.
A manifest does not override current user requirements, accessibility, platform semantics, or verified runtime evidence.
implementation: Read PROJECT_FRONTEND_CONTEXT.md when it exists before changing an established interface.
Record only project-owned evidence: source paths, captures, tests, component or token locations, platform constraints, confirmed interaction rules, and deliberate avoid patterns.
Label each entry observed, inferred, rejected, or unresolved; do not store raw prompts, named people, private messages, credentials, or another product's protected expression.
Keep the manifest small enough to resolve a real implementation choice, and update it only after an inspected result or an explicit product decision.
verification: Each claimed rule links to a current file, capture, test, or named decision instead of a vague style label.
A reviewer can tell which parts are evidence, inference, and explicit exceptions.
A narrow change can preserve the listed tokens, component contracts, platform behavior, and accessibility constraints without a broad rewrite.
accessibility: Record keyboard, focus, semantic, reduced-motion, and high-contrast constraints as behavior, not cosmetic preferences.
responsive: Include the responsive order, content limits, and breakpoint behavior that the project has already proved.
performance: Name existing dependency, hydration, media, and motion constraints so a refinement does not add avoidable cost.
browser_notes: Document platform-specific material or input behavior as a constrained enhancement with an honest fallback.

title: Make consequential frontend changes from a scoped contract
principle: Before a consequential existing-UI change, state the exact target, outcome, must-preserve behavior, permitted acquisition boundary, evidence recipe, and rollback boundary so implementation remains a refinement rather than an accidental redesign.
rationale: A visible request often touches routes, state, focus, data, dependencies, and platform behavior beyond the named selector. A small contract exposes that scope before changes spread.
applies_when: A task changes an existing route, shared component, interaction, visual system, motion behavior, or external component dependency.
exceptions: A typo or isolated CSS correction may use the same checks mentally without creating a separate artifact.
A target that cannot be located is a discovery blocker; do not infer a broad replacement scope.
implementation: Name the route, component, selector, or state being changed and the visible outcome the user should observe.
List behavior, URLs, data, accessibility, state, and platform rules that must remain true.

For any external primitive or catalog candidate, record canonical source, license and entitlement, dependencies, accessibility and state coverage, performance cost, and the safer native or maintained alternative before installation.

Choose a proportionate evidence recipe: affected state fixtures, keyboard path, reduced motion, relevant viewport, runtime or screenshot observation, console or network evidence when relevant, and focused regression checks.
Define a recoverable rollback boundary such as the focused diff, feature flag, migration step, or prior component contract.
verification: The target resolves to an existing route, file, component, or runtime state before implementation begins.
Matching before/after states demonstrate that listed invariants still hold.
The completion report separates source, runtime, packaged or deployed, and user-visible evidence rather than claiming one proves all layers.
Unrun evidence and blockers remain visible.
accessibility: The contract always includes the affected control's name, keyboard path, focus behavior, errors or status, and reduced-motion outcome when relevant.
responsive: Include content-driven widths, zoom, touch or pointer behavior, and source order when the target can reflow.
performance: Treat new libraries, media, hydration, animations, and third-party requests as explicit tradeoffs rather than free visual polish.
browser_notes: Use an explicit rendered-ready condition and user-facing locators for dynamic browser proof; do not substitute source inspection or a fixed delay.
